title: Tetris DS
subtitle: Falling blocks meet Nintendo history
summary: Tetris DS is Nintendo's handheld puzzle collection placing the familiar falling tetrominoes beside characters and imagery from its earlier games. body: Tetris DS is Nintendo's handheld puzzle collection placing the familiar falling tetrominoes beside characters and imagery from its earlier games. Standard play uses a Super Mario Bros. theme, while the other modes draw on series including Zelda, Metroid and Donkey Kong. The Nintendo DS hosts several variations on arranging blocks, with local multiplayer supporting a particularly large group. The collection gives the established rules a lively surrounding cast without losing the immediate purpose of fitting the next piece into a stack that must remain under control.

Standard mode continues the familiar cycle of moving and rotating a descending tetromino to complete horizontal lines. Each placement changes what the following piece can do, making the shape of the remaining gaps as important as the line just cleared. The pace rises as progress continues. Tetris DS also allows a piece to keep rotating before it locks, offering more time to reconsider a difficult position. The surrounding Nintendo animation supplies another visual rhythm, while the player's attention remains on the changing relationship between the current piece and the growing stack.

Local play supports up to ten participants, while Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection originally offered online contests for as many as four. Competitive items add another source of disruption to the task of maintaining a clear playing field. The collection's six single-player modes provide alternative rules and themes when players want a different kind of puzzle. Together, these arrangements turn the cartridge into several ways of returning to the same set of shapes, allowing a solitary attempt to improve a score and a noisy group contest to share a recognisable foundation.
